## Judgment

### Expected-drift set
consumers.sh core-microvm-host lists sweet16 (already imports the key, config unchanged) and petunia (newly imports it via hosts/petunia/default.nix). lock-diff.sh 9d16c83..HEAD reported no flake.lock changes. Only petunia is expected to drift; sweet16, avina, hermes, groot@dualie and groot@forge must be identical. groot@rk3588 is N/A on x86_64 and excluded.

### Actual vs expected
The sets are equal. verify-drift.sh shows DRIFT only for petunia. sweet16, avina, hermes, groot@dualie and groot@forge are identical. Derivation inspection (nix derivation show, recursive input diff, plus per-option nix eval on both revs) shows petunia's change confined to the microvm module:
- system-path gains bridge-utils, virtiofsd and waypipe, and nothing else (no input drv is removed or swapped).
- New units unit-microbr-netdev.service and network-addresses-microbr.service, plus 40-microbr.link. The bridge is microbr at 192.168.33.1/24.
- networking.networkmanager.unmanaged changes from [] to interface-name:microbr and interface-name:microvm*.
- networking.nat.enable changes from false to true with internalInterfaces = [microbr] and externalInterface = null. This adds nixos-nat firewall chains to the firewall start, stop and reload scripts.
- modprobe.d/nixos.conf gains exactly one line, `options kvm_amd nested=0`.
- udev rules gain the kvm group rule and the microvm-host-nested-check RUN hook.
- boot.kernelModules gains nf_nat_ftp, a side effect of enabling NAT.
- The initrd, boot.json, etc, activate and dbus/polkit restart-trigger drvs differ only as downstream consequences of the above. The initrd embeds the modprobe.d config.
The kernel (linux-cachyos-server-7.2.8) and zfs derivations are unchanged: neither appears among the differing input drvs. kernelParams, ZFS modprobe options and the docker daemon settings (zfs storage driver) are identical.
Docker conflict review: the NixOS NAT rules live in their own nixos-nat-pre and nixos-nat-post chains, separate from docker's DOCKER chains. The masquerade covers only 192.168.33.0/24 from the microbr interface, which does not overlap docker's default 172.17.0.0/16. networking.nat also enables ip_forward, which docker already requires. The firewall is iptables-based (nftables.enable = false) and trustedInterfaces and checkReversePath are unchanged. No functional conflict was found from evaluation. This is not a runtime test. The firewall unit restarts at switch and briefly reloads iptables rules, so check docker container connectivity after a deploy.
